provenance.method: Representation Router planning-review principles applied to the views already built and approved for the scene viewer; records the choice, not a tool-generated score or visual certification. No sketch set was put to Brian for these views.

question: Can Brian see, on a shared run, where each person went, what they tried, which rule allowed or refused it and why, and how the whole world's parts connect?
rationale: Where people are and which door stopped them is a spatial question, so the room map is primary; which rule and which things a try used is a relation question, so the graph is a switchable overlay and its own page for worlds without rooms. A round slider keeps one moment selected across both.

compositionPlan.primary_element: Room map at the selected step
secondary_elements: Show rules tags (allowed / refused with the failed check)
Show graph overlay (people tags, moves and things used)
Whole-system graph page for any shared run
People panel with each person's action in words
compositionPlan.interaction: Step slider, play/pause, Show rules, Show graph, Every box, wheel zoom, drag pan, Reset view; read-only, no model call.
compositionPlan.color: Blue allowed, orange refused, grey no move, always with words.

alternatives: A table of tries per round answers what happened but not where; kept in the people panel and the shared-run view.
The Network panel's force graph was a tangle at 70 boxes and 411 links (roadmap/README.md:63); replaced by the three-column graph.
